summary.text: The Mesozoic Era lasted from about 252 to 66 million years ago and is made up of the Triassic, Jurassic and Cretaceous Periods.
Known as the Age of the Dinosaurs, it had a hot greenhouse climate and saw the supercontinent Pangaea break apart.
It began after the Permian–Triassic extinction and ended with the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction, which killed off the non-avian dinosaurs.

items.prompt: The name Mesozoic means 'middle life'. Middle of what?

options.label: It sits between the Paleozoic and Cenozoic eras
It falls halfway through Earth's whole history
It sits between two ice ages of equal length
Its animals were midway in size between others

items.explain: The Mesozoic is the middle of the three eras since complex life evolved, after the Paleozoic ('old life') and before the Cenozoic ('new life').

items.prompt: The first, archaic birds appeared in the Jurassic. Which group did they evolve from?

options.label: Flying reptiles called pterosaurs
Small gliding mammals
A branch of theropod dinosaurs
Early crocodile relatives

items.explain: Archaic birds evolved from a branch of theropod dinosaurs in the Jurassic, and true toothless birds followed in the Cretaceous.

items.prompt: Mammals already lived alongside the dinosaurs. What were they like during the Mesozoic?

options.label: Large grazers the size of cattle
Top predators that hunted dinosaurs
Ocean giants as big as whales
Small animals, under about 15 kg

items.explain: The first mammals appeared in the Mesozoic but stayed small, under 15 kg, until the Cenozoic.

items.prompt: You take a walk through a Jurassic landscape. What kind of plants would mostly surround you?

options.label: Flowering trees and meadows of flowers
Gymnosperms such as conifers, cycads and ginkgoes
Wide open plains of grass
Only mosses, since trees had not evolved

items.explain: Gymnosperms like cycads, ginkgoes and conifers dominated; flowering plants appeared only in the Early Cretaceous and later replaced them.

items.prompt: What marks both the beginning and the end of the Mesozoic?

options.label: The formation of a new supercontinent
The start and end of a great ice age
A mass extinction event
The first appearance of a new animal group

items.explain: The era began in the wake of the Permian–Triassic extinction and ended with the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction.

items.prompt: In the Triassic, deserts filled the interior of Pangaea. As the land masses split and seas opened between them, how did the Early Jurassic climate compare?

options.label: It was tropical and much more humid
It was even drier, with deserts spreading
It turned icy, with glaciers on every continent
It stayed exactly as it had been

items.explain: In the Early Jurassic the climate was tropical and much more humid than the Triassic, because of the large seas between the land masses.
